article_title: Learning Analytics and Computational Techniques for Detecting and Evaluating Patterns in Learning: An Introduction to the Special Issue
citation: Taylor Martin & Bruce Sherin. (2013). Learning Analytics and Computational Techniques for Detecting and Evaluating Patterns in Learning: An Introduction to the Special Issue. Journal of the Learning Sciences, 22(4), 511–520. https://doi.org/10.1080/10508406.2013.840466
title: Five special issue articles demonstrating supervised, unsupervised, and process-characterizing learning analytics across science inquiry, programming, interview, and tutoring data
description: The article summarizes the special issue's contributions as demonstrations of LA method classes. Gobert et al. use supervised classification of log files labeled via text replay tagging to detect students designing controlled experiments in Inq-ITS. Berland et al. use unsupervised methods on program snapshots from the IPRO environment to propose "a framework of three phases of learning to program: explore, tinker, and reﬁne." Sherin automates discovery of student conceptions in interview transcripts; Baker et al. study learning curves in the Genetics Cognitive Tutor; Blikstein et al. associate patterns of program changes with course performance.
requirements: Each article's method requires feature selection or similarity decisions by the analyst, as described for supervised and unsupervised approaches.
constraints: The fifth article, by Blikstein et al., could not be included in the issue due to page limitations and appears in a future issue of JLS.
target_learners: Middle school, high school, and college learners studied in the contributing articles
target_learning_goals: Detecting inquiry skills, programming pathways, student conceptions, and learning-curve patterns from process data
examples: Four of the five articles attempt to characterize unfolding learning processes in a substantial way, using methods such as hidden Markov models.
